threads.subject: How the best PMs run discovery

messages.body:
The Product Weekly, issue 212

This week: how the best PMs run discovery.

We interviewed product leads at eight companies between 20 and 200 people about how they decide what to build next. Three patterns showed up everywhere.

1. They talk to customers on a schedule, not when they have a question. Five conversations a week was the median.
2. They write the problem down before the solution, and share the problem write-up with engineering before any mockup exists.
3. They kill more than they ship. The best teams had a graveyard doc and were proud of it.

Full piece on the site, about an 8 minute read.

Also this week: a template for a one page problem brief, and a reader question about pricing experiments.

threads.subject: Seed Signals: October round-up

messages.body:
Seed Signals, October round-up

Round sizes are up and round counts are down. Median seed in our tracked set was $3.4M this month, against $2.9M in October last year, with about 15% fewer deals closed.

What founders are telling us:

Term sheets are taking longer. The median from first meeting to signed term sheet was 41 days, up from 33.

Pro rata is back on the table. Two thirds of the term sheets we saw this month included some form of pro rata rights, and about a quarter extended them past the next round. Push back on that one if you can.

Option pools are being negotiated harder, with 10% post-money still the most common ask.

On the site this week: a founder's annotated term sheet, and a comparison of three data room tools.

Seed Signals is free. Forward it to a founder who needs it!

threads.subject: Stack Notes #148: the cost of a flaky test suite

messages.body:
Stack Notes, issue 148

The cost of a flaky test suite

We instrumented CI at six companies for a month. Average time lost to re-running flaky tests was 4.2 engineer hours per week per team, or about one engineer in ten doing nothing. Fixing the top 5% of flaky tests eliminated 80% of the retries.

Also in this issue:

A short write-up on moving a 40-service deployment from cron-based jobs to a queue, including what broke.

Postgres connection pooling for serverless, with the numbers on what a 6 connection cap actually means at load.
